headline: Oil back over $100 into a two-day inflation print
standfirst: Two sessions of selling on energy-driven inflation fear, a 10-year yield at a three-year high, and hike odds near 60% going into the Fed's blackout. PPI lands 08:30 ET today, CPI tomorrow.

bullets.title: The tape has been risk-off for two days, and the reason is oil
bullets.text: Brent settled at $101.21 and WTI at $96.05 after renewed US–Iran hostilities, with Brent back above $100 for the first time since July. The Dow lost more than 600 points Tuesday and over 400 more Wednesday; the S&P fell 0.5% and the Nasdaq 100 0.3% on Wednesday. This is not a growth scare — it is an inflation scare arriving four days before an FOMC meeting.

bullets.title: Rates are the transmission mechanism to watch
bullets.text: The 10-year yield touched roughly 4.85%, its highest since late 2023, and did so even as the Treasury announced it will buy back up to $6bn of 10- to 20-year debt today. A buyback that fails to pull yields down is a signal in itself. If yields press higher through the release, index futures have been following.

bullets.title: The market is pricing a hike, and the Fed is not united
bullets.text: CME FedWatch has been showing roughly 60% odds of a 25bp increase at the 15–16 September meeting, up sharply after a strong August payrolls report. DBS notes officials went into the blackout period divided on whether to move. A hawkish surprise in today's or tomorrow's data has an unusually direct path into price.

bullets.title: Futures are flat-to-firm into the number
bullets.text: Early Thursday the Dow was up about 0.34%, the S&P about 0.19% and the Nasdaq 100 close to unchanged. That is positioning, not conviction. A quiet pre-market ahead of a release that the whole week has been building toward usually means thin liquidity above and below.

bullets.title: Dollar soft, gold firm
bullets.text: The dollar index has been drifting around 98.70 despite the hawkish repricing, and gold has pushed up near $4,408 on the softer dollar rather than on the geopolitics. Worth noting the divergence: if the dollar were confirming the rate story, gold would not be where it is.

calendar.note: Headline expected around 5.3% year-over-year from 4.7%; core around 4.6% from 4.2%. The high-impact release of the session.
Same print time as PPI, so it will be read through PPI rather than on its own.
Second-tier, but lands inside the New York morning window.
Moves EUR and can set the tone for the dollar before the US data.
Oracle and Adobe matter for Nasdaq breadth into Friday.
Headline seen holding at 3.4%, core easing to 2.4%. The bigger of the two.

sessionNote: Two 08:30 releases and an ECB decision before the bell is a poor morning for assuming a clean opening range. If your model needs the first fifteen minutes to be orderly, this is a day where waiting for the reaction to settle costs you very little and saves you the fake move.
watchOut: The single trap today is treating the 08:30 spike as displacement. A release-driven wick through a level is not the same as a sweep with intent behind it, and models built on liquidity runs misfire badly on data prints. If your playbook does not have a rule about trading around scheduled releases, today is the day to add one.

archive.headline: Oil tops $100, Dow sheds 400 more
archive.summary: Brent broke $100 for the first time since July and the 10-year yield hit a three-year high. Amgen fell over 10% on a failed cardiovascular trial and software names sold off. Fear and Greed stayed in the Fear zone. Barclays nonetheless lifted its year-end S&P target to 7,950.

archive.headline: Weekend strikes push energy up, futures down
archive.summary: A weekend exchange between the US and Iran lifted energy and pulled index futures lower. Strong August labour data pushed September hike odds above 60%. New Canadian tariffs added a second inflation channel.
